reason: The potato trough needs a low-power way to circulate water, and the spare circulator looks suited to it.
expectation: I expect the circulator to provide gentle water movement for the potato roots, though I don't know exactly how it will connect.

alternatives.reason: The felt and hose may make a passive watering arrangement, but I want to equip a trough directly first.
The lamp also needs attention, but keeping the roots watered seems like a useful first step.

effect: The potato bed now has reserve-powered circulation that keeps its roots supplied with water and air. The lettuce bed still needs a low-power arrangement.
reaction: It is satisfying that the pump fits the existing loop and preserves the potato cover and support.
reason: The felt and hose may make a passive watering arrangement for the lettuce trough, so I want to prepare that next.
expectation: I expect a wick or hose assembly that can move water toward the lettuce roots, though I do not know how it will connect.

alternatives.reason: The lamp also needs preparing, but I want to address water for both beds first.

effect: The felt and hose made a wick intended to connect the lettuce reservoir to its root bed. It still needs to be fitted to the trough.
reaction: The hose sleeve holding the felt without pinching it is a useful detail.
reason: Fitting the wick should give the lettuce bed its low-power water supply.
expectation: I expect the wick to draw water from the reservoir into the shallow root bed without a pump.

alternatives.reason: The lamp also needs attention, but I want to finish supplying water to both beds first.

effect: Both beds now have low-power watering, and the lettuce wick keeps the granules moist without flooding the air spaces.
reaction: The distinction between moist and flooded roots is useful.
reason: The only available combination addresses the remaining goal of lighting the leaves.
expectation: I expect the foil to help direct the lamp's light toward the plants, though I don't know how it will be fitted.

effect: The foil and lamp made a hooded growing lamp, ready to be mounted in the nook.
reaction: Nothing notable yet; the result does not explain how the hood affects the light.
reason: Mounting the lamp is the only available combination and should address the remaining lighting goal.
expectation: I expect the lamp to provide some light to the sheltered plants, though I don't know how much.

effect: The mounted lamp directs its limited light toward both troughs, completing the garden's low-power survival setup.
reaction: The small pool of light around the plants is a memorable image, and the hood's purpose is now clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the lettuce wick was most worthwhile: it showed how solution can reach roots while leaving air between the granules.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the hooded lamp felt least engaging on its own because the result did not explain the hood until the lamp was mounted.

surprise.text: The hose sleeve held a felt wick in place without pinching it, an arrangement I had not anticipated.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the lamp hood's effect was unclear when it was first made.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see whether the garden and the preserved core make it through the storm, especially after setting up the beds for survival.
